samples.evidence: The anchor is `{ path: [0,0], tag: 'span', fp: 'deadbeef' }`. samples.summary: No test covers stampSource when two JSX-returning functions share a name
samples.evidence: `findJsxRoots` overwrites `roots[name]` on collision (only reporting via `ambiguous`), and stampSource iterates `Object.entries(roots)`, so with two `Row` functions in one file only the last one's elements get stamped — the first component's nodes are silently unclickable. jsx-nodes.test.mjs covers ambiguity for `resolveNode` and `findJsxRoots`, but stamp.test.mjs never uses `ambiguous` or a duplicate-name fixture (searched the whole file for a second same-named function).

samples.summary: No test that a non-static / conditionally-rendered node still RESOLVES when requireStatic is not set
samples.evidence: The refusal messages say "only layout-props is" — i.e. attribute edits on iteration-scope and `{…}`-owned nodes are supposed to succeed. Every test touching those cases (jsx-nodes.test.mjs 'blocks structural edits on a conditionally-rendered node', 'refuses structural edits in an iteration scope', 'still blocks... reached through {…}') passes `{ requireStatic: true }`. Nothing asserts `resolveNode(sf, anchor)` with no opts returns `located: true` for those nodes, so an over-broad guard that refused them unconditionally would not be caught.

samples.summary: The "drift guard" test derives its expectation from the same walkJsx the code under test uses, so it pins nothing about the numbering itself
samples.evidence: `expectedIds()` (stamp.test.mjs:26-38) calls `findJsxRoots`/`walkJsx` — exactly what `stampSource` calls. The comparison catches re-derivation inside stamp.mjs but is invariant to any change in jsx-nodes numbering. The only literal pinning is the four `toContain` ids plus `stamped.length > 10` at line 118, an arbitrary bound; the KITCHEN_SINK id list is never written out, so e.g. a change that renumbered fragment children would leave both sides in agreement and green.

finding.evidence: The anchor is `{ path: [0,0], tag: 'span', fp: 'deadbeef' }`. The node at [0,0] is `<b id="one"/>`, whose fp is a real digest, so `at.fp === anchor.fp` is already false and no entry matches `fp: 'deadbeef'` in either search step. verdict.reason:
Verified against the repo. The test at jsx-nodes.test.mjs:380-384 passes anchor `{path:[0,0], tag:'span', fp:'deadbeef'}` against src `
` (line 354), where [0,0] is the real `` (confirmed by the candidates `[[0,0],[0,1]]` assertion at line 397). In resolveNode (jsx-nodes.mjs:670) the guard is `if (at && at.tag === anchor.tag && at.fp === anchor.fp)`. Since `fp` is an 8-hex digest produced by fpOf (line 538; format asserted at test line 321), the literal 'deadbeef' does not equal the node's fp, so the `at.fp === anchor.fp` conjunct is already false and the fallback fpx/fp searches (lines 676-677) match nothing, returning located:false. Removing `at.tag === anchor.tag` leaves the test green, so the assertion is vacuous with respect to the tag guard it names. No other resolveNode call in the file (lines 366, 375, 394, 403, 410, 423, 440, 453, and selfResolve at line 56) pairs a real fp with a mismatched tag, so the tag comparison is untested. Vacuous test presented as coverage for a named guard = major under the test-adequacy rubric.

verdict.reason:
Verified in-repo. resolveNode (src/server/jsx-nodes.mjs:675-677) does `uniq(fpx matches) ?? uniq(fp matches)`, so the fpx step is only observable when fp is ambiguous but fpx is unique. The test 'relocates via a unique fpx when the path hint is stale' (test/server/jsx-nodes.test.mjs:363-370) uses `
`; since fpOf (line 578-588) hashes tag + sorted attrNames + IDENTITY_ATTRS (which includes `id`, line 65-68), the `` entry's fp is already unique among the three entries, so the fp fallback alone yields the identical result (`located`, same path, `relocated: true`). Deleting the entire fpx branch leaves this test and the sibling test at line 372 green — the test name claims coverage it does not provide. I read the whole resolveNode describe block (353-457) and grepped every `fpx` occurrence under packages/design-editor/test: no test constructs fp-ambiguous/fpx-unique (trivially available since fpOf deliberately excludes className content, so two siblings with different classNames share an fp), and no test exercises the documented reverse fallthrough of a stale fpx falling through to a unique fp (src line 599-604). The ambiguity test at 386-399 uses byte-identical siblings, ambiguous under both keys, so it also passes without the fpx branch. Real behavior with no test that can fail if it breaks: major under the test-adequacy rubric.

finding.evidence: `parseDiagnostics` is an @internal TypeScript property, absent from the public `ts.SourceFile` typings. The test file is plain `.mjs` with no `// @ts-check`, so nothing catches it if the property is renamed/removed or not populated; the `?? []` then turns every one of these into `expect([]).toEqual([])`, which passes for arbitrarily broken stamped output — including the type-argument splice test at line 158, which is the only guard on the `attributes.pos` offset choice. verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. `packages/design-editor/test/server/stamp.test.mjs` uses `expect(parse(text).parseDiagnostics ?? []).toEqual([])` at lines 149, 158, 173 and 228 — line 149 runs once per each of the 8 fixtures (lines 136-147) and line 228 runs once per each of the 4 bad paths (line 224), so ~14 executions of an assertion whose only failure mode depends on an undocumented property. `parse()` is `ts.createSourceFile(...)` (packages/design-editor/src/server/jsx-nodes.mjs:56-58), and `parseDiagnostics` is indeed an @internal TS property, not part of the public `ts.SourceFile` typings; the file is plain `.mjs` with no `// @ts-check` (line 1), and nothing anywhere in the package positively proves the property is populated (grep for `Diagnostic` across packages/design-editor returns only these four lines). The `?? []` fallback therefore does convert the assertion into `expect([]).toEqual([])` if the property is ever absent, with no test asserting that deliberately malformed source yields a non-empty array. I could not settle the factual crux from this repository: `node_modules` is not installed (no `typescript/lib` present), so I could not verify at any citable file:line whether `createSourceFile` actually attaches `parseDiagnostics` at runtime — my belief that it does is knowledge-based, not repo-grounded, which is not enough to clear the refutation bar. One sub-claim is demonstrably overstated: line 158 is NOT the only guard on the `attributes.pos` offset choice — line 157 positively asserts `text` contains `'<Select<string> data-wb-node="C:0"'`, which fails if the splice lands at `tagName.end`. That weakens but does not eliminate the finding, since the remaining ~13 "still valid source" assertions rest solely on the masked property. Keeping the finding.
